Chapter 14: Healing, Joy, and the Practice of Self-Care
After everything we've been through, it’s so easy to lose sight of joy, isn’t it? For Black women, healing isn’t just about getting by—it’s about finding ways to truly thrive, to celebrate, and to let yourself rest without guilt.
Picture this: a woman strolling through the park, sunlight warming her face. She laughs with friends, dances to her favorite song, maybe even treats herself to something special. Moments like these? They aren’t trivial. They’re powerful acts of resistance, especially in a world that so often tries to dim her happiness.
Most folks don’t realize just how radical it can be to put yourself first—to choose self-care. The world keeps pushing for endless giving, endless strength. But here’s the thing: rest, pleasure, and creativity aren’t luxuries. They’re absolutely essential for healing. They give you the fuel to keep moving, to keep fighting, to keep dreaming big.
Healing isn’t a straight road. There are bumps, setbacks, days when hope feels miles away. But then, out of nowhere, you hit a breakthrough. You find a bit of clarity, forgiveness, or even peace. Those moments matter.
What really stands out is this: joy isn’t some distraction from the hard work of justice—it’s actually a core part of it. When you care for yourself, you’re honoring the ancestors who paved the way, and you’re making space for the generations still to come.
So, every moment of rest, every burst of laughter, every act of self-kindness—it’s more than just self-care. It’s a way of healing, and a way of building a better future.
